scope: Primary-source reading only; no new robot experiment or implementation

sources.title: Visual Servo Control, Part I: Basic Approaches
verified_sections_pages: The Basic Components of Visual Servoing, PDF pp. 1-2 (printed pp. 82-83)
verified_facts: Image features s from image measurements are compared with desired features s* to form error e.
A velocity control law uses an estimated image interaction matrix to turn feature error into camera velocity.
The paper distinguishes image-based features from 3D position-based features; no universal control frequency is stated here.
sources.replan_or_observe: Repeated image-feedback control; fixed Hz not specified in the cited section
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: Not an action-chunk algorithm; separate emergency cancellation interface is not specified
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: Conceptually compatible when features are computed from own/top RGB and known camera calibration; current UGRP must not inject ground-truth pose
sources.applicability: Direct control-law analogy for PairNavigator.decide and rigid_pair_commands, not a ready-made carried-payload controller

sources.title: ViNT: A Foundation Model for Visual Navigation
verified_facts: Input is current and five past RGB observations plus a subgoal image; model predicts temporal distance and a future action sequence.
Action space is relative waypoints normalized by robot top speed; a robot-specific controller tracks un-normalized waypoints.
Appendix Table 6 gives prediction horizon H=5.
The CARLA fine-tuning evaluation uses a 4 Hz image context, a goal image 1.5 seconds ahead on a demonstration graph, and a simple PID tracker.
sources.output_type: 5 future relative waypoints, not direct motor voltage
sources.replan_or_observe: 4 Hz RGB context is reported for a CARLA experiment, not a universal deployment frequency
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: PID can adjust low-level tracking; paper does not specify a universal mid-sequence cancellation contract
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: RGB and static goal/map design are conceptually compatible; CARLA goal-node selection/localization and pretrained model are not automatically available in UGRP
sources.applicability: Short relative waypoint and robot-specific tracking architecture

sources.title: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
verified_facts: Policy input is recent RGB observations and optionally an RGB goal image; it outputs a distribution over future actions.
Fig. 2 depicts five past observation steps and eight future actions.
Long-horizon navigation is combined with a topological graph and frontier-based subgoals.
The checked paper does not give a fixed control Hz, exact executed prefix length, or a mid-chunk cancellation API.
sources.output_type: 8 future navigation actions sampled by action diffusion; paper does not give physical units in cited section
sources.replan_or_observe: Exact deployment refresh cadence not specified in checked paper
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: RGB input is conceptually compatible, but training/validation on UGRP carried-load dynamics would be new work
sources.applicability: Reference for RGB-conditioned short action sequences; exploration mechanism is lower priority for an authored static map

sources.title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
verified_facts: The VLM emits intermediate spatial language commands, such as moving forward 75 cm, and a separate locomotion policy executes them.
The paper explicitly describes slow VLA and real-time low-level policy as two timescales but does not give their control Hz.
For Go2, LiDAR point clouds are broadcast at 15 Hz; this is a sensor frequency.
Examples map discrete VLM words to 0.5 m/s forward or ±π/6 rad/s turn commands, with durations aligned to the VLM output.
Low-level actor observes LiDAR-derived height map and proprioceptive history including orientation and joint state; these exceed current UGRP student input permissions.
sources.output_type: VLM spatial language instruction -> command velocity -> desired leg joint positions
sources.replan_or_observe: Two timescales; exact VLM/low-level loop Hz not reported in checked passage
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: Low-level policy reacts to its own sensors; high-level mid-command cancellation guarantee not specified
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: Architecture only; LiDAR height map and measured joint/proprioceptive input cannot be passed to UGRP student controller
sources.applicability: Separate high-level instruction from ongoing low-level visual control

sources.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
verified_facts: ACT observes four cameras and measured follower joint positions, then predicts target joint positions for both arms.
Basic action chunking observes once and executes k steps; temporal ensembling instead queries the policy every timestep and combines overlapping predictions.
The 5 Hz versus 50 Hz result belongs to a human teleoperation study, not a required ACT inference or navigation observation rate.
sources.replan_or_observe: Every k steps for basic chunking, every timestep for the temporal-ensemble variant
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: Basic chunk has no interim policy update; temporal-ensemble variant incorporates fresh observations; emergency stop API not specified
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: Original ACT observations use measured joint positions and therefore are not directly admissible for UGRP student execution
sources.applicability: Action overlap and incremental corrections are transferable ideas, but method and task are manipulation-specific

sources.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
verified_facts: At timestep t, the policy takes To recent observations and predicts Tp future actions, commits to only Ta actions, then replans.
The action execution horizon is a trade-off between smoothness and reaction speed.
Real-world Table 7 entries include Ta=6 and Ta=8 steps, with prediction horizon Tp=16; these are step counts, not seconds or Hz.
The paper evaluates manipulation, usually position control, not loaded two-robot navigation.
sources.output_type: future robot action sequence, predominantly position targets in cited physical experiments
sources.replan_or_observe: After the executed Ta-step prefix; no universal seconds/Hz in cited result
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: Policy does not replan during Ta-step committed prefix; hardware emergency cancellation is not established or denied by the paper
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: Control structure can inspire an RGB/own-command-history variant, but original policy data/action space are not a drop-in fit
sources.applicability: Short receding horizon with explicit step-count versus wall-time distinction

sources.title: Real-Time Execution of Action Chunking Flow Policies
verified_facts: Asynchronous inference starts while the current chunk is still executing, instead of waiting at the boundary.
The new chunk freezes the already committed prefix and inpaints later actions for cross-chunk continuity.
Algorithm 1's controller gets a new observation each Δt and returns the next current-chunk action; a background inference loop replaces the chunk when ready.
The paper cites π0's 50 Hz target and 20 ms Δt as a particular VLA example, not a generic RTC rate.
The method assumes a flow/diffusion action-chunk policy; it is not a direct inpainting method for UGRP's rule-based PairNavigator.
sources.output_type: continuous action chunk from flow/diffusion policy
sources.replan_or_observe: Observe each controller Δt; overlap computation and execution; update after next chunk is ready
sources.mid_chunk_observation_and_cancellation: Observations arrive during current execution; next chunk can replace it when ready; protective stop contract is not provided for UGRP
sources.ugrp_allowed_input_fit: Scheduling pattern could fit allowed RGB/history, but published policy/robot observations and inpainting are not directly transferable
sources.applicability: Only pursue asynchronous pipeline if measured inference delay, rather than physics/render work, causes motion stalls
